source_text:
Ὁμοίως πάντες ἐντρεπέσθωσαν τοὺς διακόνους ὡς Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ὡς καὶ τὸν ἐπίσκοπον ὄντα τύπον τοῦ πατρός. τοὺς δὲ πρεσβυτέρους ὡς συνέδριον θεοῦ καὶ ὡς σύνδεσμον ἀποστόλων. χωρὶς τούτων ἐκκλησία οὐ καλεῖται.
περὶ ὧν πέπεισμαι ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἔχειν. τὸ γὰρ ἐξεμπλάριον τῆς ἀγάπης ὑμῶν ἔλαβον καὶ ἔχω μεθ̓ ἑαυτοῦ ἐν τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ ὑμῶν, οὖ αὐτὸ τὸ κατάστημα μεγάλη μαθητεία, ἡ δὲ πραότης αὐτοῦ δύναμις: ὃν λογίζομαι καὶ τοὺς ἀθέους ἐντρέπεσθαι.
ἀγαπῶν ὑμᾶς φείδομαι, συντονώτερον δυνάμενος γράφειν ὑπὲρ τούτου. οὐκ εἰς τοῦτο ᾠήθην, ἵνα ὤν κατάκριτος ὡς ἀπόστολος ὑμῖν διατάσσωμαι.
thought_title: Honor deacons, elders, and bishop as God's order
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the church in Tralles, urging them to honor their deacons, elders, and bishop as the visible order of God.
pass_a_gloss: Likewise let all respect the deacons as Jesus Christ, as also the bishop being a type of the Father. And the elders as a council of God and as a bond of the apostles. Without these a church is not called. Concerning which things I am persuaded that you hold thus. For I received the pattern of your love and I have it with me in your bishop, whose very disposition is great discipleship, and his gentleness is power; whom I consider that even the godless respect. Loving you I spare you, being able to write more intensely about this. Not for this did I think, that being condemned as an apostle I should give orders to you.

choices.why: The imperative with πάντες carries the force of a command to the whole community; 'respect' captures the reverent deference Ignatius demands toward church officers.
τύπος is a technical term for a representative figure; 'type' preserves the theological sense that the bishop images the Father.
σύνδεσμος means a binding link; 'bond' keeps the metaphor of the elders as the connective unity of the apostolic body.
The passive of καλέω here means 'is not named/called a church'; the literal rendering preserves the definitional force of Ignatius's claim.
rejected: it cannot be called a church

choices.why: ἐξεμπλάριον is a loanword from Latin exemplarium, meaning a model or copy; 'pattern' conveys the exemplary quality of the Ephesians' love embodied in their bishop.
κατάκριτος means one under sentence; 'condemned' captures Ignatius's status as a prisoner awaiting execution.

pass_b_english: In the same way, let everyone respect the deacons as they would Jesus Christ, just as they should also respect the bishop, who is a pattern of the Father, and the council of elders as the council of God and as a bond of the apostles. Without these, a church is not called a church.

I am persuaded that you already hold this view. For I received the pattern of your love and I have it with me in your bishop, whose very disposition is a great discipleship and whose gentleness is power. I consider that even the godless respect him.
Because I love you, I am sparing you, though I could write more sharply about this matter. I did not think that, being condemned, I should give you orders as if I were an apostle.

problems.quote: I believe that even the godless respect him.
problems.source_quote: ὃν λογίζομαι καὶ τοὺς ἀθέους ἐντρέπεσθαι.
problems.why: Greek says the godless should be corrected (reproved), not that they respect him.
problems.fix: I consider that even the godless should be corrected.
problems.ruling: ἐντρέπεσθαι here means 'to be put to shame' (middle voice); the godless are shamed by the bishop, not respecting him.

edits.old: I believe that even the godless respect him.
edits.new: I consider that even the godless should be corrected.

problems.why: Same office rendered three ways; readers may think 'elders' and 'presbyters' differ from 'council of elders.'
problems.fix: Use one term consistently, e.g., 'council of elders' throughout.

edits.old: I consider that even the godless should be corrected.
edits.new: I consider that even the godless respect him.

fixed: The glossary issue about 'council of elders' is not a translation error in this passage; the English already uses 'council of elders' consistently here, so no edit is needed.
The previous edit 'should be corrected' was wrong; the source means the godless respect the bishop, so I have restored 'respect him.'

problems.why: Same Greek presbyterion rendered with and without parenthetical 'presbyters', risking confusion.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note.

problems.quote: council of elders in the place of the council of the apostles
problems.why: Same word 'council' used for presbyterion and apostolic group, but different Greek words may be involved; still risks conflation.
problems.fix: Note Greek terms or use 'college of apostles' if distinct.

problems.why: Same office rendered two ways; readers may think presbyters are a different group.
problems.fix: Use one term consistently or add '(presbyters)' once.

edits.old: and the council of elders as the council of God and as a bond of apostles.
edits.new: and the council of elders as the council of God and as a bond of the apostles.

fixed: The glossary problems concern the literal gloss, not the English translation. The English consistently uses 'council of elders' for presbyterion and 'council of God' for the divine council, so no change is needed in the English. The gloss has been adjusted to include the article 'the apostles' to match the source.

problems.why: 'Council of elders' is standard, but 'council of the apostles' and 'council of the bishop' appear once each; reader may miss these are the same institution.
problems.fix: Use consistent 'council of elders' with note where source differs.

problems.why: The 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' are analogies for the elders, but may read as separate bodies.
problems.fix: Clarify these are analogies: 'council of elders—which corresponds to the council of the apostles.'

edits.old: who is a type of the Father
edits.new: who is a pattern of the Father

fixed: The English 'council of elders' is correct and consistent with the glossary; the source uses 'συνέδριον θεοῦ' and 'σύνδεσμον ἀποστόλων' as analogies, not as separate institutions, and the English already renders them as 'the council of God' and 'a bond of the apostles,' which is accurate.
The source 'τύπον τοῦ πατρός' means 'pattern' or 'image' of the Father, not 'type' in the sense of category; changed to 'pattern' to match the Greek sense.
The English already presents 'council of God' and 'bond of the apostles' as analogies for the council of elders, so no clarification is needed.

last_rejected.quote: I am persuaded that you hold this view already.
last_rejected.source_quote: περὶ ὧν πέπεισμαι ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἔχειν.
last_rejected.why: Greek says Ignatius has persuaded them; English flips to say they already hold the view.
last_rejected.fix: I have persuaded you to hold this view.
last_rejected.ruling: πέπεισμαι ὑμᾶς οὕτως ἔχειν = 'I am persuaded that you [already] hold this'; no agency flip, just standard rendering.

last_rejected.quote: let everyone respect the deacons as they would Jesus Christ
last_rejected.source_quote: πάντες ἐντρεπέσθωσαν τοὺς διακόνους ὡς Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν
last_rejected.why: ἐντρεπέσθωσαν means “let all correct/admonish,” not “respect”; the phrase “as they would Jesus Christ” misrepresents the comparative construction.
last_rejected.fix: Let everyone correct the deacons as one would correct Jesus Christ.
last_rejected.ruling: ἐντρεπέσθωσαν ὡς Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν naturally means 'respect as Jesus Christ'; 'correct' is less common but respect is valid range.

polish.changed: Clarified that the council of elders is the same body throughout, made the bishop's qualities the subject of the second sentence, and smoothed the final sentence's word order for natural modern reading.

notes.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered differently; 'council of the apostles' and 'council of God' may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' as metaphor.

notes.why: Same body rendered three ways; reader may miss they are identical.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; gloss others as metaphors.

polish.changed: Clarified that the elders are the same body throughout, kept every claim and qualification, and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.why: Same Greek word (presbyterion) rendered as 'council of elders' but also 'council of the bishop' and 'council of the apostles', which may confuse readers about whether these are the same body.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; note 'council of the apostles' is a different metaphor.

notes.why: In 2.6, elders stand 'in the place of the council of the apostles'—but 'council of the apostles' is not the same as 'council of elders', though both use 'council'. Reader may conflate them.
notes.fix: Clarify that 'council of the apostles' is a separate metaphor for the apostolic college.

notes.why: Unique phrase 'council of the bishop' in 5.8; elsewhere always 'council of elders'. Reader may wonder if this is a different body or a mistake.
notes.fix: Verify Greek; likely should be 'council of elders' or add note explaining this variant.

notes.why: Same office rendered four ways; 'council of God' and 'council of the bishop' could be mistaken for different bodies.
notes.fix: Use 'council of elders' consistently; reserve 'apostles' for the apostles.

polish.changed: Clarified that the council of elders is the same body as the elders, made the bishop the clear subject of the respect clause, and smoothed the final sentence so the contrast between Ignatius's condemned status and apostolic authority is easier to follow.

notes.why: Same institution alternates between 'council of elders' and plain 'elders'; reader may think these differ.
notes.fix: Use consistent term or gloss as 'body of elders/presbyters'.

notes.why: Same office rendered two ways; reader may miss equivalence.
notes.fix: Use one term consistently or note equivalence.
